subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's layered pre-auth device-signature mitigation, including protocol caps and a new per-IP signature bucket, once current-head proof is supplied?
rationale: The diff is a security fix but changes pre-auth authentication failure semantics and protocol validation bounds, which are compatibility- and security-boundary decisions that should not be accepted by automation alone.

options.title: Review after current-head proof
options.body: Require a fresh live run against 6640657f559fcffcdf890ada96a5ca393344d047, then have a gateway/security owner review the lockout and compatibility semantics before merge.

options.title: Accept the current proof
options.body: A maintainer can decide the older live proof is enough because the central CPU-DoS mitigation did not change, accepting the unproven latest response-path change.

options.title: Replace with a narrower fix
options.body: If the schema caps or response semantics are too broad, ask for a smaller PR that only gates signature verification before crypto and preserves existing error contracts.

recommendation.title: Review after current-head proof
recommendation.body: Require a fresh live run against 6640657f559fcffcdf890ada96a5ca393344d047, then have a gateway/security owner review the lockout and compatibility semantics before merge.
